question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

AV : EA :: EC : ? :: SY : WD
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. IH.

GIVEN

• AV : EA :: EC : ? :: SY : WD

SOLUTION

• Find the rule from AV → EA: A(1)+4=E(5); V(22)+5=A (22+5=27→1). So rule = 1st letter +4, 2nd letter +5.

• Verify with SY → WD: S(19)+4=W(23); Y(25)+5=D (25+5=30→4=D). ✓

• Apply to EC: E(5)+4=I(9); C(3)+5=H(8) = IH.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Add +4 to the first letter and +5 to the second letter of the given cluster.

NOTE

• Fix positions A=1…Z=26 and wrap past Z back to A (mod 26); confirm the rule on a known pair before applying.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , QE, NA, KW, HS, EO, BK, YG
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. TI.

GIVEN

• ? , QE, NA, KW, HS, EO, BK, YG

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Q, N, K, H, E, B, Y → each −3 (Q17→N14→K11→H8→E5→B2→Y25). Term before Q = Q(17)+3 = T(20).

• 2nd letters: E, A, W, S, O, K, G → each −4 (E5→A1→W23→S19→O15→K11→G7). Term before E = E(5)+4 = I(9).

• Missing term = TI.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the series backwards: first letters go −3, second letters go −4; step one place before QE.

NOTE

• In two-letter series, split into two independent columns and find each column's common difference.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

WQ, TK, QE, NY, KS, HM, ?, BA
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. EG.

GIVEN

• WQ, TK, QE, NY, KS, HM, ?, BA

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: W, T, Q, N, K, H, ?, B → each −3 (W23→T20→Q17→N14→K11→H8→E5→B2).

• 2nd letters: Q, K, E, Y, S, M, ?, A → each −6 (Q17→K11→E5→Y25→S19→M13→G7→A1).

• Missing term = EG.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Column 1 drops by 3, column 2 drops by 6; after HM comes E then G.

NOTE

• Letters wrap: after A(1) subtracting continues from Z(26); keep a mental A=1…Z=26 strip handy.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(IA, KC, NG)

(PQ, RS, UW)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (PI, RK, UO).

GIVEN

• (IA, KC, NG) and (PQ, RS, UW)

SOLUTION

• 1st letters of the three clusters: pattern +2 then +3 — IA→KC→NG: I(9)→K(11)→N(14); PQ→RS→UW: P(16)→R(18)→U(21). ✓

• 2nd letters: pattern +2 then +4 — A(1)→C(3)→G(7); Q(17)→S(19)→W(23). ✓

• Test (PI, RK, UO): 1st P(16)→R(18)→U(21) = +2,+3 ✓; 2nd I(9)→K(11)→O(15) = +2,+4 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Both columns start with a +2 gap; the first column's next gap is +3, the second column's next gap is +4.

NOTE

• For 'group of clusters' questions, test each option against the two given sets' internal pattern, not against each other.

question: What will be the sum of the number of Mondays in the months of March and May in the year 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Year 2003; count Mondays in March and in May.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2003 = Wednesday. 1 March 2003 is 59 days later; 59 mod 7 = 3 → Wed+3 = Saturday.

• March: 1st = Sat, so Mondays fall on 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 = 5 Mondays.

• 1 May 2003 is 120 days after 1 Jan; 120 mod 7 = 1 → Wed+1 = Thursday. May Mondays: 5, 12, 19, 26 = 4 Mondays.

• Sum = 5 + 4 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month gives 5 of the 3 weekdays it starts on; March starts Sat → Mon has 5, May starts Thu → Mon has 4.

NOTE

• 2003 is not a leap year (Feb = 28); use days-elapsed mod 7 to jump to any month's 1st weekday.

question: What was the last day of the year 1997?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Wednesday.

GIVEN

• Find the weekday of 31 December 1997.

SOLUTION

• Odd days = 1600(0) + 300(1) + 97 years.

• 97 years = 24 leap + 73 ordinary → 24×2 + 73×1 = 121 odd days; 121 mod 7 = 2.

• Total odd days = 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 → 0=Sun, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 3=Wednesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Last day of a year has the same weekday as its 1 January; count odd days up to the full year 1997 → 3 = Wednesday.

NOTE

• Odd-days: 100 yrs=5, 200=3, 300=1, 400=0; each leap year adds 2, ordinary adds 1.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternative based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a hexagon carrying the number 5.

GIVEN

• Pentagon(in square) : same pentagon with '4' :: Hexagon(in square) : ?

SOLUTION

• The inner shape's number = (number of sides) − 1.

• 1st pair: pentagon has 5 sides → number = 5 − 1 = 4 (as shown). ✓

• 3rd figure is a hexagon (6 sides) → number = 6 − 1 = 5.

• So the missing figure = hexagon containing 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Count sides of the main shape and subtract 1 to get the number written inside.

NOTE

• In figure analogies first check simple numeric links (sides, corners, lines) before hunting for rotations.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the box rotated 90° clockwise.

GIVEN

• Figure-1 (letters F/P/R/S) : Figure-2 :: Figure-3 (symbols) : ?

SOLUTION

• Figure-1 → Figure-2 is a 90° clockwise rotation (F top→right, P right→bottom, R bottom→left, S left→top). ✓

• Apply the same 90° clockwise turn to Figure-3: each symbol shifts one position clockwise and itself turns 90° CW.

• Result: left-arrow on top, down-arrow on left, square-dash on right, circle-dash at bottom = Option 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the left pair's turn from the letters, then spin the symbol box the same way — 90° clockwise.

NOTE

• When rotating, remember both the position AND the orientation of every element change together.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LP290 : MI404 :: KT310 : ? :: AZ810 : WX924
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QH424.

GIVEN

• LP290 : MI404 :: KT310 : ? :: AZ810 : WX924

SOLUTION

• Rule for letters: reverse the two letters, then subtract 3 from each. LP → reverse PL → P−3=M, L−3=I = MI. ✓ (AZ → ZA → Z−3=W, A−3=X = WX ✓).

• Rule for number: +114 (290→404, 810→924).

• Apply to KT310: reverse KT → TK → T−3=Q, K−3=H = QH; 310+114 = 424 → QH424.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Swap the letters, drop each by 3, and add 114 to the number.

NOTE

• Always test the derived rule on the second given pair (AZ810→WX924) before choosing the answer.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LAD110 : MBE230 :: KCH150 : LDI270 :: VUS180 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. WVT300.

GIVEN

• LAD110 : MBE230 :: KCH150 : LDI270 :: VUS180 : ?

SOLUTION

• Letters: each letter +1. LAD→MBE (L+1=M, A+1=B, D+1=E) ✓; KCH→LDI ✓.

• Number: +120 (110→230, 150→270).

• Apply to VUS180: V+1=W, U+1=V, S+1=T = WVT; 180+120 = 300 → WVT300.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift every letter one step ahead and add 120 to the number.

NOTE

• Uniform +1 shifts are common; verify with a second pair so you don't confuse it with a reversal rule.

question: In a certain code language, 'STORY' is coded as '95' and 'TOUR' is coded as '72'. How will 'RATE' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 42.

GIVEN

• STORY = 95, TOUR = 72; find RATE.

SOLUTION

• Take the sum of letter positions and subtract 2.

• STORY = 19+20+15+18+25 = 97; 97 − 2 = 95 ✓.

• TOUR = 20+15+21+18 = 74; 74 − 2 = 72 ✓.

• RATE = 18+1+20+5 = 44; 44 − 2 = 42.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Code = (sum of A=1…Z=26 positions) − 2.

NOTE

• When a positional sum is 'close but off', check for a fixed add/subtract constant across all given words.

question: In a certain coded language 'CHEER' is coded as 'DIIBM' and 'SALTS' is coded as 'TBPQN'. How will 'POLLS' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. QPPIN.

GIVEN

• CHEER = DIIBM, SALTS = TBPQN; find POLLS.

SOLUTION

• Positional shifts (letter 1→5): +1, +1, +4, −3, −5.

• Check CHEER: C+1=D, H+1=I, E+4=I, E−3=B, R−5=M = DIIBM ✓ (SALTS→TBPQN ✓).

• POLLS: P+1=Q, O+1=P, L+4=P, L−3=I, S−5=N = QPPIN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the fixed shift pattern +1, +1, +4, −3, −5 and apply position-wise.

NOTE

• When two coded words give the same per-position shift, that shift set is the key — no need for a single common shift.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AZ80, ED260, IH440, ML620, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. QP800.

GIVEN

• AZ80, ED260, IH440, ML620, ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: A, E, I, M, ? → +4 each → M(13)+4 = Q(17).

• 2nd letters: Z, D, H, L, ? → +4 each (Z26→D4→H8→L12) → L(12)+4 = P(16).

• Numbers: 80, 260, 440, 620, ? → +180 each → 620+180 = 800.

• Missing term = QP800.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Both letters jump +4 and the number jumps +180 each step.

NOTE

• Treat letters and the number as three parallel arithmetic progressions.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

PRI999, JLC918, DFW837, ?, RTK675
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. XZQ756.

GIVEN

• PRI999, JLC918, DFW837, ?, RTK675

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: P, J, D, ?, R → −6 each (P16→J10→D4→X24→R18).

• 2nd letters: R, L, F, ?, T → −6 each (R18→L12→F6→Z26→T20).

• 3rd letters: I, C, W, ?, K → −6 each (I9→C3→W23→Q17→K11).

• Numbers: 999, 918, 837, ?, 675 → −81 each → 837−81 = 756.

• Missing term = XZQ756.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Every letter drops 6 (wrapping past A) and the number drops 81.

NOTE

• For three-letter series split into three columns; a constant −6 with wrap-around is easy to miss without A=1…Z=26.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 4 PM and 5 PM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 50 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 4:13.

GIVEN

• Between 4 PM and 5 PM the angle between the hands = 50°.

SOLUTION

• Angle = |30H − 5.5M|, with H = 4 → |120 − 5.5M| = 50.

• Case 1: 120 − 5.5M = 50 → 5.5M = 70 → M ≈ 12.7 → ≈ 4:13.

• Case 2: 5.5M = 170 → M ≈ 30.9 (4:31, not in options).

• So the required time ≈ 4:13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Use M = (30H ∓ angle)/5.5; here (120 − 50)/5.5 ≈ 12.7 min past 4.

NOTE

• The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute over the hour hand — the base of every clock-angle problem.

question: A clock is 4 minutes slow at 9:00 PM and 10 minutes slow at 3:00 AM (next day). At what time (in PM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5:00.

GIVEN

• 4 min slow at 9:00 PM, 10 min slow at 3:00 AM (next day).

SOLUTION

• From 9 PM to 3 AM = 6 hours, during which it loses 10 − 4 = 6 min → 1 min lost per hour.

• The clock keeps falling behind, so 'correct time' must be earlier, when it was 0 min slow.

• At 9 PM it was 4 min slow; going back at 1 min/hour, it was 0 min slow 4 hours earlier = 5:00 PM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Rate = 6 min ÷ 6 h = 1 min/h; wind back 4 min slow ÷ 1 min/h = 4 h before 9 PM = 5 PM.

NOTE

• A clock 'slowing' shows correct time only in the past instant when its error was zero.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the star with four spiky petals and one rounded petal.

GIVEN

• A 5-petal star; the figures 1→4 show 0, 1, 2, 3 petals turning from rounded blobs into spiky (V-shaped) arms.

SOLUTION

• Each step, one more petal (moving around the star) changes from a rounded blob to a pointed/spiky arm.

• Figure 4 has 3 spiky petals, so Figure 5 must have 4 spiky petals and 1 rounded petal.

• That is Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Count how many petals have already 'sharpened'; the next figure sharpens exactly one more.

NOTE

• In figure series, track a single feature (here: rounded → spiky) advancing one unit per step.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. corner arrows up with three middle triangles.

GIVEN

• Boxes with four corner arrows and a row of small ▽ triangles in the middle.

SOLUTION

• Corner arrows alternate direction each figure: up, down, up, down, so Figure 5 = up.

• Middle triangles increase 1, 1, 2, 2, 3… every two steps, so Figure 5 = 3 triangles (▽▽▽).

• Figure 5 = corners UP + 3 triangles = Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Arrows flip every figure (5th = up); triangle count rises in pairs → 5th figure has 3.

NOTE

• Handle each feature (arrow direction, triangle count) as its own independent cycle.

question: Ratio of present ages of A, B and C is 1 : 5 : 8. Difference between the ages of C and A is 35 years. What is the sum of the present ages of A, B and C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 70 years.

GIVEN

• A : B : C = 1 : 5 : 8; C − A = 35 years.

SOLUTION

• Let the ages be x, 5x, 8x.

• C − A = 8x − x = 7x = 35 → x = 5.

• Sum = 1x + 5x + 8x = 14x = 14 × 5 = 70 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Sum ÷ difference = 14 ÷ 7 = 2, so sum = 2 × 35 = 70.

NOTE

• In ratio problems, one 'part' value (x) unlocks every quantity — find it first.

question: Sum of the present ages of J, P and S is 64 years. 8 years ago from the present the ratio of ages of J, P and S was 1 : 3 : 4. What is the present age of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 23 years.

GIVEN

• J + P + S = 64 (present); 8 years ago J : P : S = 1 : 3 : 4.

SOLUTION

• Sum 8 years ago = 64 − (3 × 8) = 64 − 24 = 40.

• Ratio parts = 1 + 3 + 4 = 8 → one part = 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

• P (8 years ago) = 3 × 5 = 15 → present P = 15 + 8 = 23 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 3×8 from the total to reach the past sum, split by the ratio, then add back 8 for P.

NOTE

• For 'n years ago' with 3 people, reduce the present total by 3×n to align with the past ratio.
